what_it_does: When a language model server handles many requests at once, two latency targets matter: how quickly the first word appears (Time-to-First-Token, TTFT) and how smoothly subsequent words stream out (Time-per-Output-Token, TPOT). Existing servers use fixed rules — always prioritize new requests, or always prioritize ongoing ones — which causes one metric to routinely violate its deadline while the other has budget to spare. SOLA fixes this by watching the real-time latency state of every request and every 'batch tick,' then solving a small optimization problem each tick to decide exactly which requests to run and how many tokens to process — switching between 'fix the TPOT while not breaking TTFT' and 'fix the TTFT while not breaking TPOT' as conditions change.
method_in_detail:
The idea. An LLM server processes requests in discrete batched steps called iterations. At each iteration it can run a mix of: (a) new-request prefill (processing the full input prompt to produce the first token, which sets TTFT) and (b) decode steps for ongoing requests (generating one token per running request, which accumulates into TPOT). Existing systems pick one fixed priority rule for all iterations. SOLA instead treats each iteration as a fresh scheduling decision.

Design space. SOLA parameterizes scheduling by three variables it re-solves every iteration: Fi (a sort function that orders requests in the waiting queue), ni (max number of requests to pull into the running batch), and ki (max number of tokens to execute). These three knobs can reproduce any known scheduling policy and also reach points no prior system could.

State monitor. After each iteration finishes, SOLA updates: per-request real-time TTFT and TPOT; a system-wide summary ratio (worst real-time value / SLO threshold) for each metric; predicted remaining output lengths drawn from a distribution built from finished requests; and current memory usage.

Strategy generator. Each iteration SOLA picks which constrained optimization problem to solve: if TPOT is the more violated metric, minimize worst-case TPOT subject to TTFT staying within its deadline, and vice versa. If both are violated, it loosens the constraint progressively. The optimizer then applies two-level prioritization: first decide phase priority (prefill vs. decode), then sort within each phase by predicted deadline slack. Finally it sets ki or ni to the tightest value that satisfies the constraint (e.g. limit how many prefill tokens to add before TPOT breaks).

Cost model. A polynomial formula (coefficients tuned offline, then scaled online by a smoothed ratio of predicted vs. actual latency) predicts how long a batch will take, enabling the optimizer to set ki safely without over-committing.

The result. Implemented on top of the vLLM serving engine, SOLA raises SLO attainment from 45.5% to 99.4% on Llama3-70B with ShareGPT workloads. Across five model/dataset combinations it serves 1.04-1.27x more requests per second than state-of-the-art systems at 90% attainment, adding only 0.4-0.45% scheduling overhead.
